_comment: AGENT: always read this file via the task-index-manager skill before reading or writing any task state. System tracker for ai-worldbuilder (ADR 002). Never add tasks for individual worlds here

tasks.title: Pitched roof stairs derive shape and facing from neighbouring stairs at the same height
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-28 from the roof-stair gaps issue (I-022, snag S-029); independent review applied. Cause class: Translation. The plan chooses each stair's corner shape from height differences between columns (pitched_roof_states, lib/builds/feature_build.py about lines 699-707, which has an inner branch only for a valley where the diagonal is not higher). The game derives a stair's corner shape from stairs at the SAME HEIGHT beside it, so placed shapes differ from the plan and joins change. Not verified when written: the game's exact placement rule and order; which cells gap; whether the wall fill under each roof column (edge_wall_expose, about line 1588) leaves nothing behind a stair's open half. Deliver: (1) step one, read placed blocks to confirm the game's rule; (2) regularise heights into a buildable roof first (lidar is only a guide for roofs), then derive each stair's facing and shape from its same-height neighbours; delete the old height-difference branch (ortho_pair / diagonal block and _corner_shape), do not leave it beside the new one; (3) fill behind open stair halves only if step one shows a real gap; (4) extend the existing roof lint (lib/audit/roof_lint.py; scripts/roof_lint.py is a wrapper) to check stair shape against the rule. Files: lib/builds/feature_build.py, lib/builds/test_feature_build.py, lib/audit/roof_lint.py, rules/feature-builds.md. Related, not blocking: #125 (pitched zones), #149 (stairs, slabs and full blocks), #161 (readback ignores stair shape, so the lint must read placed blocks or the plan). Proof: unit tests on MemoryBlocks for outer corner, inner corner, valley with a higher diagonal, hip, straight run, three rises, and a slab or full block beside a stair. Check: python3 scripts/roof_lint.py on a rebuilt pitched roof shows 0 stair-shape mismatches; view one hip and one valley with no light holes; the owner's review of the roof-stair gaps snag stays the final judgement. Helps: every pitched roof (zoned features, hip roofs, houses, terraces).

tasks.title: Pitched roof stairs take the material of the roof they belong to
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-28 from the dark-stairs-in-a-brick-roof issue (I-023, snag S-030); independent review applied. Cause class: Translation. A roof column takes its material from its lidar zone alone (roof_material_for_zone, lib/builds/feature_build.py, called at about lines 1559 and 1589). zone_ridge_half_steps (about line 447) treats a whole zone as pitched when any of it rises 1 m or more, so a lower zone's material climbs the slope of a higher roof: in one rebuilt roof 363 stairs of the lower zone's material appeared and 117 of them touched main-roof columns. Not verified when written: how the eave rows land in the lower zone (the exact-tie idea in snap_to_levels is unproven and ties are rare; the nearest-level snap plus mode_filter and bucket_zones is a likelier source; no zone-grid dump yet); the roof in game. Deliver: a sloped column takes the material of the roof it rises from, not only its zone's material; the spec stays the owner of zone_materials; no old path is removed, only the zone-only lookup. The tie-break change is out of scope; file it separately only if a zone-grid dump shows ties happen. Files: lib/builds/feature_build.py (roof_material_for_zone and its callers, zone_ridge_half_steps), lib/builds/test_feature_build.py (already has the snap test), and the zone_materials text in rules/feature-builds.md. Related: #126 (zone materials), #125 (pitched zones). Blocked by the roof stair task (#169) because both touch the pitched-zone code path. Proof: unit tests with two zone levels asserting each column's material. Check: re-run the dry run for the zoned feature in the snag and count stairs of the lower zone's material that touch only main-roof columns (expect 0), and look at the roof in game. Helps: any zoned pitched feature that gives each zone its own material.

tasks.title: Roof details are checked for solid roof under them before they are placed
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-28 from the glass-hangs-over-the-roof-edge issue (I-025, snags S-032 and S-044); independent review applied. Cause class: Capability. _validate_details (lib/builds/feature_build.py about line 1116) checks only types and shapes; _place_detail (about line 2411) places each box blindly; _solidify_roof_under (about line 2393) only swaps slab, stair, carpet or trapdoor blocks that already exist below, so air below stays air. Designers copy aerial rectangles against slanted roof edges, so boxes hang over the edge: on one rebuilt building 5 of 12 skylight blocks and 6 of 16 solar-panel blocks had air beneath. Across the specs of one world, 18 specs carry 105 roof detail rows, 59 of them skylights, and none is checked. Deliver: (1) after the roof is built, test each cell of a roof detail box (every kind in ROOF_DETAIL_KINDS) for a full, slab or stair block at the level below; air does not count; (2) clip the unsupported cells out of the box; (3) the dry run prints one line per row with unsupported cells (label, kind, position, count); (4) add 'a roof detail sits on solid roof; cells over air are clipped' to rules/feature-builds.md and rules/building-review.md (this covers the designer brief); (5) move or shrink the one existing spec row that overhangs, or confirm the new check clips it. Out of scope: refusing a build (it would block all 18 specs). Proof: unit tests on MemoryBlocks (a fully supported box is unchanged; a box over a diagonal edge is clipped; the dry-run line is present). Check: python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only test_feature_build passes; the dry run for the feature in the snags lists the clipped row; after a rebuild, block_scan_region finds no glass block with air at the level below. Related: the issue that skylight rows sit one block above the roof instead of opening it (I-033) is a different cause and still passes this check. Helps: all roof detail kinds on every feature.

tasks.title: Decor places permanent lidar-detected objects, using photo plus lidar to skip vehicles
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-28 after the I-026 rebuild (#172 landed). Cause class: Capability. Ground now builds bare terrain only, so objects the lidar sees above it (surface minus terrain: planters, kiosks, bins, bollards, cars) are built by nothing: decor_plan and street_furniture use only map, aerial and designer plans and never read lidar. Deliver: decor takes lidar object columns outside footprints and trees, groups them into objects, and places one only when a street photo or the aerial identifies it as permanent furniture; vehicles and other transient objects are dropped by design (a parked car must not be built). Owner's rule: needs photo plus lidar together to place objects and avoid cars. Check decor_plan/street_furniture for an existing photo or aerial classification step to reuse before adding one. Proof: a unit test where a lidar object column with a permanent-furniture label is placed and one labelled vehicle is not. Related: #172, I-026. Helps: every ground pass on a lidar baseline.

tasks.title: Door build places the entrance cover (awning_like) from the facade plan
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-28 from the SUSU entrance covered-area issue (I-021, snag S-027; also the covered-entrance part of I-018). Cause class: Capability. facade_plan entrances accept and validate awning_like (lib/builds/facade_plan.py) but plan_doors in lib/builds/feature_build.py never reads it; awning_like is only built from free-standing details rows. Not verified: what the SUSU portal photos show at each entrance. Deliver: after the shell and roof are built (as details() does, so the roof pass does not overwrite it), a cover is placed over each placed entrance whose awning_like.kind is not none. Two geometries: awning and covered_area = a row of roof-material bottom slabs at door top + 1, as wide as the door leaves plus 1 block each side, extending out `depth` blocks over the step-out (depth default 1 when absent or 0; covered_area simply uses the larger depth, no wall carving); porch_roof = the same slab roof plus a post at each outer front corner standing on the step-out ground. Cells inside the building mass are skipped; the door stays walkable. Unresolved entrances and kind none build nothing. Dry-run prints `door <id> cover <kind> depth <n>`. Files: lib/builds/feature_build.py, colocated tests in lib/builds/test_feature_build.py (one per kind, none builds nothing, depth changes extent, unresolved entrance builds no cover, existing details awning_like row unchanged), rules/feature-builds.md (geometry per kind, plan_doors reads it). The spec edit that adds awning_like to the SUSU entrance (susu_w33830305) is part of the check, not the code change: the designer or rebuild adds it after reading the photo. Check S-027: after rebuilding susu_w33830305 with an awning_like entry on its entrance, a roof stands over the door in game and the door is still walkable.
